_what_this_is: The pinned rules an MS2 molecular-networking campaign grades against. Every number here is part of gold's definition rather than a parameter of the comparison, and each was chosen before the ladder was written -- see the T-L4-2 grounding section in docs/npbench-c.md for what was measured and what the measurements retired.

network.peak_tolerance_note: In Da, and the same value the dereplication template pins, for the same measured reason: the aggregate barely moves across the plausible range while individual answers do.
network.edge_rule_note: An edge joins two node spectra whose cosine is at least the threshold AND which share at least this many matched peaks. Both halves are the classical molecular-networking convention; the peak floor is what stops a two-peak coincidence from becoming an edge. No top-K neighbour cap and no component-size cap are declared, and that is a measurement rather than an omission: on this node set the threshold alone leaves no component large enough to need one. A denser node set needs both, and would be a different instantiation rather than a change here.
network.threshold_grid_note: R4's axis. The edge rule is a cut through a continuous similarity, so the campaign grades the whole cut rather than one value: every structural number moves monotonically across this grid.
network.edge_scores_are_not_graded: The pairs are graded and the scores are not. A cosine is a float out of a BLAS-backed library -- byte-identical under this image's pinned numpy and scipy, and moved in the third decimal when those versions changed -- so the pair set is the robust claim. Measured on this node set: no pair score sits within 1e-4 of any declared threshold except one, 5.6e-05 below 0.9, which is still three orders of magnitude above the float noise.

annotation.precursor_window_note: A library spectrum is a candidate for a node when its precursor m/z is within this window, in Da, of the node's. The same filter the dereplication template declares.
annotation.ranking_rule: Candidates are ordered by score descending, then matched-peak count descending, then accession ascending. The third key is not cosmetic: equal scores occur and a rule that stopped at two keys would make the answer depend on the order matchms happened to return.

confidence.note: A declared mechanical class: the first row whose score floor AND matched-peak floor the top match meets. MassBank's own CONFIDENCE field cannot do this job -- fewer than a hundred of the release's records carry it.

annotation.accepted_note: Only an accepted annotation seeds the network. The tier below it exists so that R4 can drop one tier and ask what the network's annotation coverage then looks like.

propagation.rule: A node with an accepted annotation of its own is `annotated_directly`. Otherwise look at its neighbours that carry one: none, and it is `no_annotated_neighbour`; two or more naming different compounds, and it is `conflicting_neighbours`; all naming the same compound, and the claim is `same_compound` when the precursor difference to the best-scoring such neighbour is within the annotation window and `analogue_with_mass_shift` otherwise.
propagation.note: This is what a network is for and where it is dangerous. The `analogue_with_mass_shift` claim says the node is a relative of the named compound and reports the signed shift; the `same_compound` claim says it IS that compound. The grounding measured both against the truth and the asymmetry is the campaign's finding -- see docs. Neither claim is graded against the truth: a system cannot read it, and what is graded is the claim the declared rule makes.
propagation.mass_shift_note: A shift is a difference of two shipped precursor values, so it is exact arithmetic over the inputs rather than tool output, and it is reported at the precision the records carry.
